note: Ps35 (59 spans). Appeal vs unjust foes. nefesh thread (threatened v4,7,17,25 / rejoicing v9 / afflicted-self v13). samach rejoice (foes gloat v15,19,26 / righteous-delighters rejoice v27). David mourned FOR enemies when sick (v13-14). tsedeq/chaphets close (God delights in servant's welfare). Poetic ledger; span-id pairs.

dims.v: 'TAKE HOLD (chazaq) of shield and buckler and rise for my help!' — God summoned as a warrior; chazaq the grasping of arms, the psalmist calling God to take up weapons in his defence
addressed by God's word of salvation
'Say to my SOUL (nefesh), I am your salvation!' — the inner self longing for God's assuring word; nefesh here the person craving the direct pledge of rescue (first of the psalm's many nefesh)
'I am your SALVATION (yeshuah)' — God's own word of rescue to the soul; yeshuah (recurs v9) the salvation God himself declares, the assurance the soul asks to hear
'Let them be put to SHAME (bosh)... who seek after my life' — shame invoked on the life-seekers; bosh (recurs v26) the disgrace prayed on the persecutors
'and DISHONOUR (kalam)' — humiliation invoked with shame; kalam (recurs v26) the disgrace joined to bosh, the twin fate prayed on the foes
life / soul (nefesh - who seek my life)
'who seek after my LIFE (nefesh)' — the life the foes hunt; nefesh here the life targeted (as Ps31:13), the object of the persecutors' pursuit
'Let them be turned back and DISAPPOINTED (chapher) who devise evil' — the schemers frustrated; chapher (as Ps34:5, there negated of the godly) here invoked on the evil-plotters
'who DEVISE (chashab) evil against me' — the plotting of the foes; chashab (recurs v20; as Ps21:11) the calculating malice, here scheming evil, doomed to be turned back
'who devise EVIL (ra) against me' — the harm the foes plan; ra (recurs v12) the evil purposed against the innocent, the content of their scheming
life / soul (nefesh - dug a pit for my life)
'without cause they dug a pit for my LIFE (nefesh)' — the unprovoked trap; nefesh here the life snared without cause, the innocence of the persecuted underscored
know (yada - when he does not know it)
negated ('when he does NOT know it')
'Let destruction come upon him when he does not KNOW (yada) it' — the foe caught unawares by his own trap; yada negated, the schemer surprised by the ruin he prepared for another
'Then my SOUL (nefesh) will rejoice in the LORD' — the same soul that was threatened (v3,4,7) now rejoicing; nefesh here the delivered self exulting in God's salvation, the turn from lament to joy
'my soul will REJOICE (gil) in the LORD' — the exultation of the rescued; gil (recurs Ps32:11) the joy in God that answers the soul's earlier peril
'EXULTING (sus) in his salvation' — gladness in God's rescue; sus (as Ps19:5 of the sun) here the soul's joy in the salvation God declared (v3)
'exulting in his SALVATION (yeshuah)' — the rescue that occasions joy; yeshuah (recurs v3) God's deliverance, now realised and celebrated

'delivering the POOR (ani) from him who is too strong' — God the rescuer of the weak; ani (recurs Ps34:6) the afflicted whom God saves from the overpowering foe, the incomparable deliverer 'who is like you?'
'the POOR (ani) and needy from him who robs him' — the afflicted rescued from the plunderer; ani doubled, the vulnerable God defends
'the poor and NEEDY (evyon)' — the destitute God saves; evyon = the beggar/needy, paired with ani, the helpless whom God rescues from robbers
'MALICIOUS (chamas) witnesses rise up' — witnesses of violence; chamas (recurs Ps25:19, 27:12) here the false accusers whose testimony is violence, asking of things David does not know
know (yada - things I do not know)
negated ('things that I do NOT know')
'they ask me of things that I do not KNOW (yada)' — false charges of unknown matters; yada negated, the innocence of the accused who knows nothing of what he is charged with
'They repay me EVIL (ra) for good' — the ingratitude of the foes; ra returned for kindness, the injustice that leaves the soul bereft (esp. after David's mourning for them, v13-14)
'evil for GOOD (tovah)' — the good David showed, returned as evil; tovah the kindness (his intercession, v13) betrayed, deepening the injustice
'my SOUL (nefesh) is bereft' — the desolation of the betrayed; nefesh here the self bereaved/forlorn at being repaid evil for good, deep inner loss
'BEREFT (shekol)' — bereavement of soul; shekol = childlessness/loss, the forlorn desolation of the betrayed spirit

'I AFFLICTED (anah) myself with fasting' — David's self-humbling for his enemies when they were sick; anah = to humble/afflict the soul, the astonishing compassion that fasted and prayed for those who now repay him evil

'I afflicted MYSELF (nefesh) with fasting' — the soul disciplined for the enemies' sake; nefesh here the self David humbled in intercession for those who hated him, love returning good for anticipated evil

'I PRAYED (tefillah) with head bowed on my chest' — intercession for the sick enemies; tefillah (as Ps17:1) the prayer David offered for those who now gnash at him, the height of returning good for evil

'as one who LAMENTS (qadar) his mother, I bowed down in mourning' — grief for the enemies as for closest kin; qadar = to go about in dark mourning, David treating the sick foes as friend, brother, mother — the depth of his compassion the psalm sets against their cruelty

'But at my stumbling they REJOICED (samach) and gathered' — the foes' malicious glee; samach (first of the enemy-joy thread, v15,19,24,26) the wicked gladness at David's fall, the opposite of his mourning for them
know (yada - wretches I did not know)
negated ('wretches whom I did NOT know')
'wretches whom I did not KNOW (yada) tore at me' — attacked by strangers; yada negated (recurs v11), the assailants unknown to him, their hostility unearned
'like PROFANE (chaneph) mockers at a feast, they gnash at me' — the godless scoffers; chaneph = impious/profane, the irreverent mockers whose teeth-gnashing shows their savage contempt
life / soul (nefesh - my precious life from the lions)

'Rescue... my precious LIFE (nefesh) from the lions!' — the one and only life pleaded for; nefesh here 'my only one', the precious life David begs God to snatch from the lion-foes ('How long will you look on?')
'I will THANK (yadah) you in the great congregation' — the vow of public thanksgiving; yadah (recurs Ps30) the gratitude promised amid the throng once rescue comes
'in the mighty throng I will PRAISE (halal) you' — praise vowed before the assembly; halal (recurs v27) the public praise joined to thanksgiving
rejoice (samach - let not the foes rejoice)
paired with those who hate without cause
deprecated ('Let NOT those rejoice over me')
'Let not those REJOICE (samach) over me who are wrongfully my foes' — the foes' gloating prayed against; samach (second of the enemy-joy thread) the malicious joy David asks God to forbid
'who are WRONGFULLY (sheqer) my foes' — enmity founded on lies; sheqer (recurs Ps31:18) the false ground of their hostility, hating him without cause
hate (sane - who hate me without cause)
'those who HATE (sane) me without cause' — causeless hatred; sane (recurs Ps34:21) the groundless enmity, hatred without provocation (a phrase Jesus applies to himself, Jn15:25)
peace (shalom - they do not speak peace)
'they do not speak PEACE (shalom), but... devise words of deceit' — hostility masked in speech; shalom (recurs v27) withheld, their words deceit against the quiet in the land
against the quiet in the land
'they DEVISE (chashab) words of deceit' — plotting against the peaceable; chashab (recurs v4) the scheming that targets 'those who are quiet in the land', malice against the harmless
'words of DECEIT (mirmah)' — the deceitful speech devised; mirmah (recurs Ps34:13) the guile the foes plot against the innocent
'Vindicate me, O LORD, according to your RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq)' — vindication grounded in God's justice; tsedeq (first of the tsedeq-thread, v24,27,28) the divine rightness on which the plea rests
deprecated ('let them NOT rejoice over me')
'and let them not REJOICE (samach) over me!' — the foes' triumph again forbidden; samach (third of the enemy-joy thread) the gloating God is asked to prevent
the seat of their gloating desire
'Let them not say in their HEARTS (lev), Aha, our heart's desire!' — the foes' inward gloating; lev here the wicked heart craving David's ruin, its secret triumph God is asked to thwart
'Aha, our heart's DESIRE (nefesh)!' — the foes' greedy appetite for his fall; nefesh here as craving/desire (cf Ps27:12), their soul's malicious wish 'we have swallowed him up'
those who rejoice at his calamity
'Let them be put to SHAME (bosh)... who rejoice at my calamity' — shame invoked on the gloaters; bosh (recurs v4) prayed on those glad at his misfortune, clothed with shame and dishonour
'and DISAPPOINTED (chapher) altogether' — abashment invoked with shame; chapher (recurs v4) the frustration prayed on the calamity-lovers
'who REJOICE (sameach) at my calamity' — the malicious glad-hearted; sameach (fourth of the enemy-joy thread) those who delight in his ruin, to be shamed
'at my CALAMITY (ra)' — the misfortune the foes gloat over; ra here as calamity/misfortune (as v19), David's suffering that the wicked celebrate
'Let them be clothed with SHAME (bosheth) and dishonour' — shame as a garment; bosheth (noun of bosh) the disgrace invoked to clothe the proud gloaters
'and DISHONOUR (kelimmah)' — reproach clothing the foes; kelimmah (noun of kalam, v4) the humiliation invoked to cover those who magnified themselves against David
delight in (chaphets - who delight in my righteousness)

'Let those who DELIGHT (chaphets) in my righteousness shout for joy' — the good joy set against the foes' malice; chaphets (first of two, v27) those who favour his vindication, whose joy is righteous (contrast the enemy-joy of v15,19,24,26)
'who delight in my RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq)' — David's vindicated right; tsedeq (second of the thread) his righteous cause in which his friends rejoice
those who delight in his righteousness
'shout for JOY (ranan) and be glad' — the righteous joy of David's friends; ranan (recurs Ps33:1) the good exultation that answers vindication, opposite the foes' gloating
'and be GLAD (samach)' — the gladness of the righteous; samach (fifth in the psalm, but now GOOD joy) — the same verb the foes used maliciously (v15) here redeemed for the friends of righteousness
delight in (chaphets - God delights in his welfare)

'Great is the LORD, who DELIGHTS (chaphets) in the welfare of his servant' — God's own delight in his servant's good; chaphets (second of two, v27) the divine pleasure (cf Ps18:19) in the servant's peace, the psalm's warm resolution
'the WELFARE (shalom) of his servant' — the servant's peace God delights in; shalom (recurs v20, where the foes withheld it) here the well-being God himself desires for his own — peace restored

'my tongue shall TELL (hagah) of your righteousness' — the tongue meditating and speaking God's justice; hagah (as Ps1:2 of meditating the law) here the continual uttering of God's righteousness, the psalm closing on unceasing praise

'of your RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq) and of your praise' — God's justice as the theme of the tongue; tsedeq (third of the thread, v24,27,28) the divine righteousness the vindicated servant proclaims all day long
'and of your PRAISE (tehillah) all the day long' — ceaseless praise closing the psalm; tehillah (recurs Ps34:1) the day-long praise of the vindicated, the note on which the long lament finally rests

v1: 'CONTEND (rib), O LORD, with those who contend with me; fight against those who fight against me!' - the opening appeal for God to take up the legal and martial case; rib = to bring a lawsuit/strive, David asking God to be both advocate and warrior against his adversaries

v5: 'Let them be like chaff before the WIND (ruach), with the angel of the LORD driving them away!' - the foes' insubstantiality; ruach here literal wind (as Ps1:4's chaff), the persecutors as weightless chaff blown off, driven by God's angel
be silent / deaf (charash - be not silent)

v22: 'You have SEEN, O LORD; be not SILENT (charash)! be not far from me!' - the appeal to the God who sees to act; charash negated, David begging the witnessing God not to keep silence, to break his apparent inaction (answering the foes' 'our eyes have seen', v21)
vindication / judgement (mishpat - Awake for my vindication)

v23: 'AWAKE and rouse yourself for my VINDICATION (mishpat), for my cause, my God and my Lord!' - the cry for God to rise and judge; mishpat = the just verdict David seeks, calling the seemingly-sleeping God to take up his cause
